chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man said to him: 'May God improve you. We have a butcher neighbor, and he brings a Jew to slaughter for him, so the Jews buy from him.' He said: 'Do not eat his slaughtered meat, nor buy from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a Christian or Jew butcher according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a specific ruling for a Christian or Jewish butcher whose meat is purchased by Jews, ruling that one should neither eat his slaughtered meat nor buy from him. This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the purity and permissibility of meat from the People of the Book in specific social and economic contexts, emphasizing both ritual validity and communal interaction. The ruling underscores the importance of verifying the source and method of slaughter when dealing with non-Muslims in a mixed community.
